page.running_head: SECT. I. PART. I. CAP. III.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~12 letters]nobis probatur : Nisi enim dixerit Fonseca formam substantialem intendi ac remitti, & per gradus certos produci, ita quidem ut posteriores gradus producantur à prioribus in materiam jam introductis, vel ex ea eductis, quod concessurum eum non crediderim, non video, qui monstret, formam esse principium generationis ejus , per quam existit, vel in-qua est. Et quidem in corporibus homogeneis, quorum formæ extensæ sunt & divisibiles, ad materiæ divisionem, rem non procedere sic probo: ponamus lapidem esse generandum, & in materiæ certam particulam primò introduci formam lapidis, illamque particulam continuâ regeneratione particularum aliarum fieri m[?] majorem, ut post intervallum aliquod saxum justæ magnitudinis evadat; Dicendum ergo Fonseca erit, primam illam formæ particulam in minimam materiæ portiunculam introductam in alias deinceps materiæ particulas introduxisse alias formæ particulas, quæ primæ parti unitæ, totam aliquam formam conflarint, cujus pars una produxerit alteram : quod partim falsum, partim Fonseca sententiam non confirmat. Falsum quidem est , quia[?] lapidis forma in unam aliquam materiæ portiunculam introducta nullam habet naturæ suæ multiplicandæ vim, ita ut alias ejusdem corporis & naturæ homogeneæ partes formæ novas possit producere, & se augere ; viventium instar: sed externa causa, quæ primò in unam materiæ portiunculam induxit lapidis formam, successivè deinceps alias quoque particulas generat: Deinde, si maximè generatio[?] hæc admitteretur, sententiam tamen Fon-seca nihil juvaret: Cum enim portiuncula lapidis no-va ge-

page.notes: Left margin: the marginal notes are cut off at the edge of the scan; only fragments show, none reliably readable, so the first note is a placeholder for them, placed at the start of the paragraph rather than beside the lines they stand against. Doubtful readings: "quia" (partly overprinted), "m" in "fieri m majorem" (likely "in"), "generatio" (overprinted mark), and "no-va ge-" at the page end, where the printed word may be split differently. Long s is transcribed as plain s; the italic "Fonseca" is marked with <i>. The paragraph continues onto the next page.
